messages:
Maya R: heads-up: seeing a p99 tail spike on prod LLM-serving this morning correlated with high KV miss rates on a subset of nodes
Liam K: got it — timeline?
Maya R: spike started ~1718272000, came back down after autoscale but p95 stayed up ~60ms -> 140ms at p99 for a 2-token avg request
Sophia T: interesting — any recent kernel/routing changes rolled this week?
Maya R: merged kernel-selection heuristic tweak in commit ab9f3 earlier today (tries to route to smaller kernels under low batch)
Ari (perf-bot): perf-regression alert: ab9f3 increased p99 by +18% in canary baseline (microbatch=8) — triggered by kv-cache pressure tests
Liam K: can we repro locally? profile with microbatch=1/4/8/16 and cold vs hot KV hit rates
Maya R: repro script: 
``
./bench --model gptx-7b --concurrency 400 --mb 8 --kv-hit 0.6 --duration 600
```
Logs:
[2026-04-13T09:23:01Z] shard-12 WARN kv-miss 0.42 evict-queue=high kernel-switch=attempted
[2026-04-13T09:23:02Z] shard-12 INFO batch-size 8 latency p95=62ms p99=148ms
Sophia T: kernel-switch=attempted is key — routing fallback might be causing kernel thrash under partial KV hit. We should capture stack traces.
Liam K: I dumped a perf trace from canary: frequent switch between cuda-kernel-v2 and cu-opt-path every ~200ms, lots of memcpy activity
Maya R: hypothesis: the kernel-selection heuristic chooses smaller kernel for low mb, but when KV misses increase, effective token length spikes and kernel choice is suboptimal causing cache churn + memcpy overhead
Ari (perf-bot): profiling summary attached: memcpy: +31% CPU time; kernel-launch overhead: +22%; kv-lookup latency p99: 12ms -> 45ms under surge
Liam K: quick test: pin kernel to cu-opt-path and raise microbatch to 16 — does p99 improve? anyone run?
Sophia T: ran short test on staging: mb=16 + pin kernel => p95 48ms p99 82ms, lower than canary. But throughput reduced ~8% due to larger batch waits
Maya R: tradeoff acknowledged: larger microbatch reduces kernel-switch overhead & amortizes memcpy, but increases queueing latency for latency-sensitive customers
Liam K: action items: rollback ab9f3 for hot clusters (Maya); add heuristic guard: if kv-miss-rate > 30% avoid kernel-fallback within 500ms window (Sophia); run mb sweep (1,4,8,16) with kv-hit 0.2/0.5/0.8 and collect p50/p95/p99 (Liam)
Sophia T: I'll prototype guard: pseudocode: 
```
if (kv_miss_rate > 0.3 && time_since_last_switch < 500ms) {
  keep_current_kernel()
}
```
Maya R: also adding a KV-pressure metric to console dashboard + alert when node-level evict-queue > threshold
Liam K: note: for latency SLOs we might expose an API knob per-customer: prefer throughput vs strict p99. Could auto-adjust mb per-customer policy
Ari (perf-bot): added ticket PERF-918 to track: rollback, heuristic, mb-sweep; assigned to Maya/Liam/Sophia
Maya R: rolling rollback to 20% of canaries now, monitoring p99
Sophia T: one more data point: when we force kv-cache prefetch for top-10 hot tokens, p99 improved by ~25% in microbench
Maya R: nice — add prefetch experiment to sweep
Liam K: timeline: mb-sweep + prefetch experiments in next 6 hours, heuristic PR by EOD, rollback complete in 30m
Maya R: thanks — will post short summary to #eng-runtime after tests. :thumbsup:
